verses.english: Linked Discourses 35.94
10. The Sixes
Untamed, Unguarded
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: “Chayime, bhikkhave, phassāyatanā adantā aguttā arakkhitā asaṁvutā dukkhādhivāhā honti.
verses.english: “Mendicants, these six fields of contact bring suffering when they’re untamed, unguarded, unprotected, and unrestrained.
What six?

verses.pali: Cakkhu, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ adantaṁ aguttaṁ arakkhitaṁ asaṁvutaṁ dukkhādhivāhaṁ hoti …pe…
verses.english: The field of eye contact brings suffering when it’s untamed, unguarded, unprotected, and unrestrained.

verses.pali: jivhā, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ adantaṁ aguttaṁ arakkhitaṁ asaṁvutaṁ dukkhādhivāhaṁ hoti …pe…
verses.english: The field of ear contact … nose contact … tongue contact … body contact …

verses.pali: mano, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ adantaṁ aguttaṁ arakkhitaṁ asaṁvutaṁ dukkhādhivāhaṁ hoti.
verses.english: The field of mind contact brings suffering when it’s untamed, unguarded, unprotected, and unrestrained.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha phassāyatanā adantā aguttā arakkhitā asaṁvutā dukkhādhivāhā honti”.
verses.english: These six fields of contact bring suffering when they’re untamed, unguarded, unprotected, and unrestrained.

verses.pali: Chayime, bhikkhave, phassāyatanā sudantā suguttā surakkhitā susaṁvutā sukhādhivāhā honti.
verses.english: These six fields of contact bring happiness when they’re well tamed, well guarded, well protected, and well restrained.
What six?

verses.pali: Cakkhu, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ sudantaṁ suguttaṁ surakkhitaṁ susaṁvutaṁ sukhādhivāhaṁ hoti …pe…
verses.english: The field of eye contact brings happiness when it’s well tamed, well guarded, well protected, and well restrained.

verses.pali: jivhā, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ sudantaṁ suguttaṁ surakkhitaṁ susaṁvutaṁ sukhādhivāhaṁ hoti …pe…
verses.english: The field of ear contact … nose contact … tongue contact … body contact …

verses.pali: mano, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ sudantaṁ suguttaṁ surakkhitaṁ susaṁvutaṁ sukhādhivāhaṁ hoti.
verses.english: The field of mind contact brings happiness when it’s well tamed, well guarded, well protected, and well restrained.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha phassāyatanā sudantā suguttā surakkhitā susaṁvutā sukhādhivāhā hontī”ti.
verses.english: These six fields of contact bring happiness when they’re well tamed, well guarded, well protected, and well restrained.”
That is what the Buddha said.
Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Mendicants, it’s just the six fields of contact
that lead the unrestrained to suffering.
Those who understand how to restrain them
live with faith as partner, not festering.
When you’ve seen pleasant sights
and unpleasant ones, too,
get rid of all manner of desire for the pleasant,
without hating what you don’t like.
When you’ve heard sounds both liked and disliked,
don’t fall under the thrall of sounds you like,
get rid of hate for the unliked,
and don’t hurt your mind <j>by thinking of what you don’t like.
When you’ve smelled a pleasant, fragrant scent,
and one that’s foul and unpleasant,
get rid of aversion for the unpleasant,
while not yielding to desire for the pleasant.
When you’ve enjoyed a sweet, delicious taste,
and sometimes those that are bitter,
don’t be attached to enjoying sweet tastes,
and don’t despise the bitter.
Don’t be intoxicated by a pleasant touch,
and don’t tremble at a painful touch.
Look with equanimity at the duality <j>of pleasant and painful contacts,
without favoring or opposing anything.
People generally let their perceptions proliferate;
perceiving and proliferating, they are attracted.
Casting aside all mental constructions of the domestic life,
wander intent on renunciation.
When the mind is well developed like this <j>regarding the six,
it doesn’t waver at contacts at all.
Mendicants, those who have mastered greed and hate
go beyond birth and death.”
